entities.summary:
Basolus (Basle) (c.555–c.620) was a French Benedictine and hermit who spent 40 years in solitude on a hill near Reims. He was born near Limoges and became a monk near Verzy before dedicating his life to contemplation and prayer. Basolus's ascetic practices and writings on spirituality influenced a generation of Christians, including St. Willibald of Corvey, who would later become a prominent missionary to the Franks. The hill where Basolus lived, known as the Col de Selle, still exists today and was a site of Christian pilgrimage during his lifetime. Basolus's teachings also shaped the spiritual practices of the Benedictine Order, which continues to this day. His legacy extends beyond his immediate followers, as his emphasis on solitude and contemplation has inspired countless generations of Christians and spiritual seekers. Basolus's life and teachings serve as a powerful reminder of the enduring power of faith and spirituality in the face of adversity.

The legacy of Basolus can be seen in the continued influence of the Benedictine Order, which has shaped the spiritual practices of countless generations of Christians. His emphasis on solitude and contemplation has also inspired countless spiritual seekers and has had a lasting impact on Western spirituality. 

Basolus's life and teachings are a testament to the enduring power of faith and spirituality in the face of adversity. His legacy continues to inspire and guide people around the world today.
